definitions.explanation: The same size as the real person or object, used especially for figures, statues, and representations.

examples.japanese: {寺|てら}に{等身|とうしん}の{仏像|ぶつぞう}がある。
examples.english: There is a life-size Buddha statue at the temple.

examples.japanese: {等身大|とうしんだい}のフィギュアが{展示|てんじ}されている。
examples.english: A life-size figure is on display.

examples.japanese: {等身大|とうしんだい}の{自分|じぶん}でいることが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It's important to be your authentic self.

examples.japanese: {美術館|びじゅつかん}には{等身大|とうしんだい}の{蝋人形|ろうにんぎょう}が{並|なら}んでいて、まるで{本物|ほんもの}の{人|ひと}のようだった。
examples.english: Life-size wax figures were lined up in the museum, looking just like real people.

notes:
Used on its own mainly in set compounds such as {等身|とうしん}の{仏像|ぶつぞう} (life-size Buddha statue) and {等身|とうしん}{像|ぞう} (life-size statue). In everyday Japanese it is almost always used in the compound {等身大|とうしんだい} (life-size). The literal meaning is physical size equal to the actual body, but it has a popular figurative use meaning "natural, authentic, unpretentious" — being one's true size without exaggeration.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {等身大|とうしんだい}の — life-size; true-to-life
- {等身大|とうしんだい}の{自分|じぶん} — one's true/authentic self
- {等身大|とうしんだい}のパネル — life-size standee/panel
- {等身大|とうしんだい}で{生|い}きる — live authentically

USAGE NOTE:
{等身大|とうしんだい}の{自分|じぶん} is a popular expression meaning to live without pretension, accepting oneself as one is. This figurative use is extremely common in self-help, personal essays, and everyday conversation.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {実物大|じつぶつだい} — actual size; similar meaning but emphasizes matching the real object, used more for objects than people
- {原寸大|げんすんだい} — full scale, actual size; more technical, often used in design and architecture
